submission.justification:
Radiator-R2 gives the highest pi/K separation at 10 GeV/c (4.78 sigma at 3 cm), but the recorded results flag it as porous with no hydrophobic treatment. That is a known aging risk (moisture uptake degrades refractive index and transmission), and the brief requires the radiator to keep its performance over the experiment's lifetime. No lifetime or aging documents were found to show R2 would pass, so I cannot accept it under that hard constraint. Radiator-R3 at 3 cm is the best remaining option at 3.76 sigma, ahead of R1 at 2.82 sigma (best at 3-4 cm). R3 has no lifetime flag in the results, but no lifetime documentation was found for it either, so its lifetime performance is unverified and should be confirmed before commitment. The 3 cm thickness is R3's best of the tested values (1-6 cm). Note the separation gap to R2 (about 1 sigma) is the cost of avoiding the aging risk.</justification>
